reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
Fridays used to carry a weight. There was an expectation baked into them — the week was over, you had earned something, you owed yourself a release. That story sold a lot of bottles. It sold me plenty. The trick is that Friday doesn't actually mean anything on its own. It's a square on a calendar. What we do with it is what makes it into something.

Eleven years in, my Fridays are pretty quiet in July. Maybe a long evening walk while it's still light. Dinner that I actually cook. A phone call with a friend who is also sober, also just living. It's not glamorous and it's not supposed to be. The glamorous version was killing me. What I have now is a Friday I remember on Saturday, and a Saturday I actually get to use.

Aristotle's point, as Durant framed it, is that we don't rise to some big moment of character. We settle into whoever we've been practicing being. Every ordinary Friday you show up sober, you're not just getting through it — you're becoming someone. Someone who can be counted on. Someone who trusts themselves. That person isn't built in the dramatic moments. They're built in the quiet ones you used to think didn't count.
reflection.meditation: What small, unremarkable choice today is quietly building the person I'm becoming?

affirmations: I am building a life in the ordinary hours, not waiting for the dramatic ones.
Today I can be counted on — by others, and by myself.
I have agency over how this day ends, and I choose to end it clear.

gratitude.prayer: I'm grateful for a Friday I'll actually remember. For friends who understand why a quiet night is the whole point. For the version of me that kept showing up long enough to get here, and for the small, unremarkable freedom of waking up tomorrow without having to repair anything.
gratitude.closing: One more day. That's the whole thing.
